recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-13823 in core unless a future work-group decision changes the transaction replacement policy again.
issue_request: FHIR-13823 was a Published FHIR-core HTTP change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that transaction reference fix-up be explicitly applied to URL/URI values as well as Resource references. The accepted resolution was to make explicit that elements whose explicit type is uri, url, or Reference can potentially be replaced when they reference something in the Bundle, while canonical elements are not replaced.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn/git commit 248f869abe209db2e9cef3f165b1fec24fc52738, whose message references GF#13823 and svn revision 13422. That commit changed source/http.html to list resource references and elements of type uri/url/oid/uuid as replaceable transaction links and to state that canonical elements are not replaced.
additional_context: FHIR-13990 raised the same ambiguity about replacing uri values and was retracted as a duplicate of FHIR-13823. The originating Zulip thread confirms the motivating MHD/DocumentReference.content.attachment.url use case and the concern that canonical URI values should not be rewritten. Later Published issue FHIR-36032 revisited this exact paragraph, kept the core FHIR-13823 rule, and clarified narrative/markdown and exact-match behavior.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope HTTP source already has a dedicated Replacing hyperlinks and full-urls section requiring servers to replace matching links in resource ids, resource references, uri/url/oid/uuid elements, and selected narrative links, while stating that canonical elements are not replaced. This satisfies the FHIR-13823 resolution after considering the later FHIR-36032 refinement.
